Atom arm shopping

Priced by what it costs to finish one arm, not by what looks cheap per unit. Cheapest-per-arm leads each row; the torque bar shows which servos can actually hold the shoulder up.

What the joints demand

The arm actuates four joints: three at the shoulder and one at the elbow. The forearm gearing is passive and takes no motor, so a complete arm is 3 strong servos plus 1 small one. Torque below is the stall figure each joint must produce in the worst case - arm straight forward and horizontal, shell fitted, and a 2x factor for punch and impact. A servo below the top bar cannot hold the shoulder up.

Pack bias checkYES - the pack-first bias inflated this category by $4.00 per arm (10-pack $10.99 vs Honbay 6-pack $6.99), a 57% overpay, and the same $4.00 for a 2-arm build.
Show the full check
The previous pass ranked on $/disc ($1.10/ea for the Seamuing 10-pack) which is the cheapest per-unit figure in the whole category and still the WORST way to buy 3. On ONE_ARM_COST the ranking inverts completely: Honbay 6-pack $6.99 and ZYAMY 5-pack $6.96 beat it outright. BUT the correction does not swing to singles either - it stops at the smallest pack. There is no single, 2-pack or 3-pack of the O20 4xM3@O14 disc on Amazon; every 2-pack sold as a '25T horn' is a straight lever arm (B07TYMNN5N verified by image, uxcell B09VXVJKXJ verified by its 28mm-length spec). The genuine floor is the 5/6-pack tier, where three listings cluster within $0.03 of each other ($6.96-$6.99). Within that tier the tiebreak is overshoot utility, and it favors the 6-pack: Honbay's 6 discs are exactly 3+3, so one $6.99 purchase fully covers a 2-arm build with zero orphans, while the $6.96 5-pack leaves 2 useless spares and needs a second pack ($13.92) for arm 2. So a pack does win here - just three sizes smaller than the previous pass chose. Note the 10-pack only becomes correct at a 3-arm build ($10.99 for 9 discs vs $13.98 for two Honbay packs).
Full analysis notes
STS3215 "$0 disc" question - answered NO, definitively. I pulled the package-contents block from three live STS3215 listings and none ship a usable 25T disc: DIYmall 12V 30KG (B0FGNSRCYT, $32.99) = "1 x STS3215 servo + 1 Set Metal Bracket"; DIYmall 7.4V 19KG (B0FGNG181T, $29.99) = "1 x STS3215 servo + 1 Set Metal Bracket"; 7.4V 14KG (B0H2PWCWN1, $26.99) = "1 x servo" only. The trap is the spec table: these listings all carry "Horn gear spline: 25T/OD5.9mm" and "Horn type: Plastic, POM", which reads like a bundled horn but describes the OUTPUT SPLINE the servo accepts, not an included part. B0H2PWCWN1 even lists "The rocker screw: M3 X 6" and still ships no rocker. Budget the disc as a separate line item; there is no $0 path. Even if a POM horn were bundled it would be the wrong part - the requirement is a metal O20 disc with 4x M3 TAPPED holes on a O14 circle, and the stock Feetech accessory is a plastic cross/round horn with clearance holes, not tapped, which will strip under arm loading. SHIPPING: every listing here shows "FREE delivery ... on orders shipped by Amazon over $35" or Prime. All six items are $6.96-$17.99, i.e. under $35 standalone. Inside a full arm BOM the order clears $35 and landed cost = list price, which is what I used for one_arm_cost. If bought alone without Prime, add shipping to every row equally (it does not change the ranking). SPEC CONFIRMATION on the winner: the O14 bolt-circle question on Honbay looked like a red flag at first - one review says "the holes are spaced about 9.5mm apart, not 14mm". Reading the full review text resolves it in our favor: "its 14mm BCD not a square pattern of 14mm." 14mm BCD is exactly the spec. 9.5-9.9mm is the adjacent-hole chord of a O14 circle (14/sqrt2 = 9.90mm), so both reviewers describe the correct part; they were measuring adjacent spacing while the listing quotes bolt-circle diameter. Same geometry is confirmed on ZYAMY, SQXBK, Seamuing and DaFuRui, so this disc pattern is an industry standard across sellers - parts are interchangeable and mixing brands across a build is safe. DELISTED since the previous pass - do not re-quote these, all now "Currently unavailable": HobbyPark 5-Pack (B07MMH8RVK), Magic&shell 5-Pack (B07KR5Q1Y9), SD Racing 2Pcs (B01F742JCU), DollaTek 5Pcs (B07F71J1Q2), Treedix 10pcs (B0875ZS9KF), Readytosky 10PCS (B08GZ5FHTX), uxcell single 19.7mm (B07NRX8DWS), 10Pcs alt (B0C68ZWRVJ). The uxcell 19.7mm single going unavailable is notable - it was the only true single-disc listing found, so the "buy 3 singles" path is closed on availability as well as on price. ALSO PRICED, not shortlisted: DaFuRui 20Pcs (B0CMX7S3K5) $17.99, correct spec (14mm spacing, 4x M3 tapped, 20mm dia) but one_arm_cost $17.99 - worst in class, only rational at a 6-arm build. ShareGoo 10PCS (B07H4SM6NF) $14.99, and it is a steering-arm product, not a disc. Prices captured 2026-08-19 and are volatile on these low-cost listings. I did not reuse any figure or image from the previous pass - the $10.99 Seamuing price was re-fetched and independently confirmed. Every one of the 6 images was freshly downloaded via curl from m.media-amazon.com, validated as JPEG (ffd8ff magic bytes), and 5 of 6 were opened and visually confirmed to show the correct part and pack count; that visual check is what caught the B07TYMNN5N lever-arm substitution, which the title and specs alone would have let through. Decision: how the horn mounts

Every disc here ships with 4 tapped M3 holes, and the printed bracket has heat-set inserts. Two ways to join them:

A. Drill the horn out to Ø3.2 recommended

Open the 4 tapped holes to 3.2 mm clearance. The screw then passes cleanly through the horn and threads only into the insert - one thread, one clamp, nothing to fight. About 10 seconds per horn with a hand drill.

B. Leave the holes tapped no drilling

The screw threads through the horn and into the insert. No prep work, but the two threads must stay in step: when they fight, the screw binds early, the horn sits proud and the joint mis-clocks.

Show the full check
NO inflation from single-size multi-packs. Amazon fastener listings have a hard price floor of roughly $5-9 regardless of piece count, so "buy fewer" is simply not purchasable. Two measured proofs from this pass: M3x40 costs $6.99 as a 30-pack but only $5.96 as a 50-pack, and M3x80 costs $8.99 as a 10-pack but only $8.26 as a 25-pack. In both cases the LARGER pack is absolutely cheaper. There is no 12-piece bag of M3x40 at $2. So preferring a 50-pack over a hypothetical 12-piece bag inflated the one-arm cost by $0.00 — that part of the previous pass was correct, and correcting it would cost money, not save it. Across both strategies the average spend per listing is $6.68-6.83, which is just the floor, not overshoot. YES inflation from multi-SIZE mega-assortment kits, by roughly $5-15 (8-25%). This is the real pack-first trap in this category. The minimum-viable kit (Twidec 1015pc, $8.99) is genuinely correct — it replaces $14.28 of M3x8 + M3x20 bags for a net saving of $5.29. But every step up destroys that gain, because the bigger kits add sizes you do not need while still missing the sizes you do. Measured counterfactuals against the $61.48 optimum: mxuteuk 2362pc at $19.99 -> $66.49 (+$5.01); ATHYUTH 840pc M3/M4/M5 at $20.24 -> $69.04 (+$7.56); KADRICK 1830pc at $27.99 -> $76.79 (+$15.31). Best single estimate if the previous pass reached for a headline mega-kit: about $7.56, or 12% inflation. Strategy comparison, both fully costed for ONE arm: (a) assortment kit + specific extras = $61.48 across 9 purchases, 12/12 requirements covered. (b) per-size small bags = $66.77 across 10 purchases, 12/12 covered. Strategy (a) wins by $5.29 (7.9%) — but only with the CHEAP kit, and only because the kit collapses exactly two line items. A kit covers 2 of 12 requirements here; the other 10 are irreducibly separate purchases either way. The genuine wins in this category are multi-SIZE assortments that collapse separate ~$7 minimum charges, not deep multi-packs of one size: the Swpeet nyloc assortment at $8.99 covers both the 6x M3 and 1x M5 nyloc in one buy versus ~$12 for two dedicated bags, and the 420pc insert assortment at $6.99 covers both 34x M3 x 4.0mm single SKU and 4x M4 versus ~$10+ for M3-only plus a separate M4 pack.

Best strength: iexcell 25pc Grade 12.9 $8.26 [B0DNSKT2TS], +$0.77 for ~4x tensile but partially threaded (20mm thread only) — check your stack-up. FALLBACK PRICED AS REQUESTED: uxcell 25pc M3 x 100mm fully-threaded 304SS rod, $13.79, in stock [https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FJRXGSC4]. The rod LOSES decisively — $13.79 vs $7.49 is +$6.30, and it also requires cutting 4 rods to length, deburring/chasing the cut threads, and 8 extra nuts to form headless double-nutted joints. Do not use the rod route; real M3x80 screws are available and cheaper. VERIFICATION METHOD AND HONESTY NOTES. WebFetch returns HTTP 500 on every amazon.com product page, so all prices were scraped directly with curl and parsed from each page's own JSON (the "displayPrice" field), cross-checked against the search-results price and the per-unit a-offscreen value. Every price in this report was read off the live listing on 2026-08-19. Availability was confirmed by the presence of #add-to-cart-button plus the #availability text — note that a naive grep for "Currently unavailable" gives FALSE POSITIVES on Amazon pages because that string appears in sponsored carousels; my first pass wrongly flagged five in-stock items and was corrected. Two caveats on stock depth: the DTGN M3x8 countersunk 50-pack [B0CQ4XFM67, $5.39] showed "Only N left in stock", and near-identical substitutes exist at $5.49 (Hordion 100pc [B0GD5C8GDX]) and $5.99 (50pc [B0H3GT3THJ]) if it sells out. Some listings hit an Amazon captcha during the run; those were retried and only successfully-parsed pages are reported. REJECTED — priced and rejected on evidence, not skipped: ATHYUTH 840pc M3/M4/M5 $20.24 (no M3x40, no M3x80, has M5x20 and M5x30 but NOT M5x25 — fails the bill); KADRICK 1830pc $27.99 and mxuteuk 2362pc $19.99 (both stop at M3x35, both cost more than the targeted route); HANGLIFE 345pc insert box $19.99 (nearly 3x the 420pc at $6.99); KADRICK 420pc inserts+screws combo $15.99 (M3 inserts only, no M4, so it does not close the insert requirement); Walfront 280pc $12.13 (button head only, 4-25mm); SVLING 750pc and the 500pc/1000pc M3 kits (all stop at M3x30). SHIPPING. No listing showed a separate shipping charge; all are Prime/FREE-delivery eligible. The full $61.48 cart also clears Amazon's $35 free-shipping threshold, so shipping is $0 even without Prime PROVIDED all 9 items are placed in one order. Splitting the buy across sessions could drop individual orders under $35 and add fees for non-Prime buyers. TWO-ARM SCALING. Strategy A scales to two arms for only +$7.49 (a second M3x80 6-pack) = $68.97 total, because every other pack already carries enough spares: M3x40 50pc covers 4 arms, M4x16 50pc covers 12, M5x25 30pc covers 30, nyloc assortment covers 4, inserts cover 2+. If a 2-arm build is at all likely, buy the iexcell 25pc M3x80 ($8.26) instead of the 6-pack up front — two arms then cost $62.25 total and you gain the 12.9 grade upgrade. WORST VALUE IN THE BILL, flagged for a manual fix: the 1x M5x25 requirement costs $7.99 (cheapest 30-pack) — 13% of the entire cart for a single screw, and no smaller listing exists. A single M5x25 from a local hardware store is typically $0.50-1.00. Buying that one screw offline drops Strategy A from $61.48 to about $54. The same logic applies less strongly to the 3x M3x8 button ($5.99) and 4x M3x8 countersunk ($5.39). IMAGES.
